title: sdlc-supervisor state.json
description: Machine state for the sdlc-supervisor framework: work items, their task graphs, lifecycle state, and per-task leases. Every write to .sdlc/state.json must validate against this schema, and every lifecycle_state transition must be checked against the state-transition validator (scripts/validate-state.mjs) before being persisted -- this schema only constrains shape, not legal transitions.

schema_version.description: Version of THIS schema's shape (semver). Bump when state.json's structure changes in a way that could break readers/writers.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the last write to this file. Optional but recommended -- the orchestrator should set it on every save.

work_items.description: One entry per tracked work item (a proposal/feature effort). Each work item owns a task graph.

lifecycle_state.description: Full lifecycle enum, validated on every transition. An agent cannot write a 'done'/'released'-equivalent status without the evidence its verification_commands require having actually produced.

task_status.description: Coarse status vocabulary, matching the wording used in a project's own PROGRESS.md-style task table legend. This is the field humans read at a glance; lifecycle_state (below) is the finer-grained, evidence-gated state used once a task has an actual task packet driving it through the formal pipeline. 'blocked' here is informational/manually-set (e.g. waiting on an external decision) and distinct from a task merely having incomplete dependencies, which is derivable from the dependencies array plus the referenced tasks' own status.

lease.description: Per-task lease: which agent/run currently owns this task, and how many attempts it has used. attempt_count feeds project.yaml's budgets.max_attempts_per_task -- once it reaches that limit, the task escalates to the orchestrator instead of being retried automatically.

assigned_agent.description: Role/name of the agent currently assigned (e.g. 'implementer', 'verifier'). null when the task is unassigned/unleased.

run_id.description: Identifier of the run/session that holds this lease. null when unassigned.

attempt_count.description: Number of attempts made on this task so far under the current (or most recent) lease. Reset only per the orchestrator's own policy, not by this schema.

id.description: Task identifier, e.g. 'SS0.1'. Referenced by other tasks' dependencies arrays.

lifecycle_state.description: null until this task has an actual task packet generated for it and enters the formal draft->...->released pipeline. Once non-null, transitions must go through the state-transition validator.

dependencies.description: Task IDs that must reach status 'done' (and, once tracked, lifecycle_state 'released') before this task can be leased to an implementer.

task_packet_path.description: Path to this task's generated task packet under .sdlc/task-packets/, once one exists. The packet itself is NOT embedded here -- state.json holds only the reference.

report_path.description: Path to this task's completion report under .sdlc/task-packets/ (or .sdlc/evidence/), once the implementer has returned one. Referenced only, not embedded.

notes.description: Free-text notes, mirroring the Notes column convention used in a project's own PROGRESS.md-style task table (e.g. dependency call-outs, spike findings).

lifecycle_state.description: Overall lifecycle state of the work item as a whole, distinct from any individual task's lifecycle_state.

tasks.description: This work item's task dependency graph -- a flat list of tasks, each carrying its own dependencies array (task IDs), so the graph is reconstructable without a separate edge list.
